changes.evidence: A broad closed oval is crossed by a level bar that extends to its left. Its height and barred-oval form do not securely distinguish upper-case Theta from the writer's lower-case theta. The first occurrence retains the case doubt; later occurrences were inspected separately.

changes.consequence: Keeps the unresolved case of the action symbol, with capital Theta first, rather than H’s certain lowercase theta.

changes.location: Axiom a, prose: punctuation after int

notes:
**Document (134-2.150.note.document).** This continuation sheet has author page 5 and archive foliation 150. It begins “deux axiomes suivants”; its final parenthesis and quotation remain open at the lower edge. No date, salutation, signature or closing appears. The sideways note runs along the left of the lower paragraph; its arrow ends beside the line beginning strictes, without an exact word anchor. It is retained as a margin note, with its visible guide reproduced in TikZ and its depleted opening left as approximately four illegible words.

**Axioms and checked consequences (134-2.150.check.normal_and_central; 134-2.150.check.restricted_action).** Axiom a gives equivariance of d for the action of L₀ on L₁ and conjugation on L₀. Axiom b gives the inner action associated with d(x₁), retaining the explicitly written d.(x₁). A targeted conditional proof check was performed: equivariance makes Im d normal; for k in Ker d, axiom b makes conjugation by k equal to Θ(1), hence trivial, so the kernel is central. Equivariance preserves this kernel. Axiom b then makes Im d act trivially on it, so the restricted action on π₁ factors through π₀. The reasoning is recorded in mathchecks/134-2_scan150.md; it interprets the displayed group-action axioms and does not decide their glyphs.

**Ambiguous antecedent (134-2.150.interpretation.action_on_all_L1).** The exact wording “L₀ opère sur L₁ en invariant π₁, et qu’il opère via π₀” is preserved. If the last clause were read as asserting factorization of the entire action on L₁, that stronger interpretation would be false: take d=id:S₃→S₃ with conjugation action. Then π₀ is trivial, yet (12) sends (23) to (13) by conjugation. The refined statement checked above concerns the restricted action on π₁; the wording may already intend that restriction. This counterexample refutes the stronger interpretation, not necessarily the author’s intended claim.

**Invariant and applications (134-2.150.claim.invariant; 134-2.150.claim.applications).** With coh. inserted above the line, the author identifies the principal invariant, “évidemment”, as the uncertainly spelled Postnikoff/Postnikuff-Sinh class α in H³(π₀,π₁). He reports meeting these structures in several situations, recently in the classification of “ordinaires” formal groups over a perfect field using affine algebraic groups, commutative formal groups and strict Gr-structures. The margin extends the formalism to an arbitrary topos, “pas seulement dans (Ens)”. The class construction and classification claims were not checked. No explicit authorial mathematical doubt occurs on this sheet; the transcription’s doubt marks are editorial assessments of ink.

**Mathematics and ink.** The three action letters were independently cropped and read, preserving Θ/θ case uncertainty at the first occurrence only. The dot in axiom b and both levels of parentheses are clear. All three readers independently inspected the six pi-family occurrences and their indices; the first pi retains its case doubt, with the remaining indices 1, 1, 0, 0, 1 read separately. The Coker/CoKer middle case remains uncertain. The small membership-adjacent point is preserved without assigning it a mathematical role. No equality, index or letter was changed to make the proof work.

**Other decisions and limits.** The cancelled sign favours s over a comma, before a separate live comma. Invariant and retomber retain uncertainty at clipped or overtraced strokes. Vais is clear. The crowded sur is preserved with an explicit alternative for a possible unreadable older layer; no independent cancelled word occurs after the preceding quotation. The accent in algébriques favours a grave and the accent in caractère favours a circumflex, both with alternatives. The punctuation after affines permits comma or semicolon. The final word favours des with du retained; no following page supplied a completion. H’s leading bracket in the marginal text is a misrepresentation of the arrow. Its joining-dash TeX in Postnikoff--Sinh is excluded as a typographic difference. No independent re-proof, computation or formal certificate was performed.
